subject: Biotechnology
title: Carrier Screening
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Carrier Screening.

hook.text: Carriers are healthy — but if two carriers have a child, the baby may inherit two broken copies. Screening catches this.

buildup.text: Expanded carrier screening tests for over 300 recessive conditions — cystic fibrosis, sickle cell, Tay-Sachs, and beyond.

discovery.text: One in three people carries at least one serious recessive disease allele — nearly everyone is a carrier for something.

twist.text: Carrier pairs can use IVF with preimplantation testing — selecting embryos without the disease before pregnancy begins.

climax.text: Ashkenazi Jewish Tay-Sachs carrier screening reduced disease incidence by 90% in one generation — genetics guiding prevention.

punchline.text: Know what you carry — carrier screening prevents inherited diseases before they start.

quiz.question: How did carrier screening reduce Tay-Sachs disease in the Ashkenazi Jewish community?
options: It cured existing patients with gene therapy
Identifying carrier couples allowed informed reproductive choices, reducing affected births by 90%
It eliminated the Tay-Sachs gene from the population entirely
